title: Due-job entries with no matching worker are skipped silently and never cleared
current: dispatchDueJobs reads up to 25 due members from the shared due-jobs index. A member whose job id isn't in the current run's worker list is skipped with `continue` and no log, and stays in the index.
evidence: Each caller passes only the workers it runs: dispatchScheduledJobs omits scheduled-post displacement when there's no subreddit, and onboarding and AutoGoal dispatch alone. Members of job types that were renamed or retired in earlier versions would also stay forever. Every skipped member still uses one of the 25 batch slots on every run.
investigate: List the members of the due-jobs index on a real installation: are any job ids unknown to the current code?
Can unknown members fill the 25-slot batch and delay real jobs?
Decide: log unknown members at warn, and remove ids the current code no longer defines (the 'no untracked jobs' rule).
tests: A due member with no worker is logged and doesn't consume a batch slot ahead of a known due job.

criticality.why: Mostly invisible waste, but a crowded index could delay real repair or deletion work.
